name: Other armed conflicts
summary: Ethiopian and Eritrean forces reportedly traded artillery fire near Badme on 11–13 Nov; control of the town is disputed
state: Ethiopian federal and Eritrean forces reportedly exchanged artillery fire around Badme on 11–13 Nov and Ethiopian drones reportedly struck Eritrean positions; ACLED said on 13 Nov that neither side controlled the town, and Eritrea's information ministry accused Ethiopia of invading on 12 Nov (Critical Threats). Federal and Tigrayan forces also clashed around Rama on 7–11 Nov, and G7 foreign ministers called for maximum restraint on 11 Nov. Interstate fighting is reported but not confirmed by either government, so the Alert is unconfirmed and Watch holds.
for_you: Anyone travelling to Ethiopia or Eritrea should check FCDO travel advice. Those most exposed are civilians in Tigray and along the Ethiopia–Eritrea border.
rubric_hit: Watch: significant deterioration (reported Ethiopia–Eritrea fire near Badme); new interstate war unconfirmed (Alert line)
why: Wars and flashpoints outside Canary's named list — such as Yemen, Haiti, Ethiopia–Eritrea, Afghanistan–Pakistan, Libya and Somalia — can escalate with little warning.
drivers: Coups, border clashes, insurgencies, state collapse, outside intervention.

rubric.alert: A new interstate war, a capital under attack, or mass-atrocity warnings in a conflict not tracked elsewhere.
rubric.watch: Crisis Group's CrisisWatch or credible reporting shows a significant deterioration in a conflict not tracked elsewhere.
rubric.normal: No conflict outside the named list is escalating sharply.
